name: Budgets and Allowable Costs
title: Budgets and Allowable Costs
answer: Budgets and allowable costs cover the money a funder agrees to provide for a project and the rules that decide which expenses that money may pay for. In an AI research proposal this spans personnel, compute, data acquisition and licensing, travel, publication fees, and indirect costs charged by the host institution. The scope is set by the specific funding call and the funder's cost policy, not by what the project would ideally like to buy.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Budgets and allowable costs cover the money a funder agrees to provide for a project and the rules that decide which expenses that money may pay for. In an AI research proposal this spans personnel, compute, data acquisition and licensing, travel, publication fees, and indirect costs charged by the host institution. The scope is set by the specific funding call and the funder's cost policy, not by what the project would ideally like to buy.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The budget rests on the proposal's work plan, the institution's accounting and grants office, and the funder's own submission system. Cost figures come from vendor quotes, institutional rate agreements, and published fee schedules, and they must be traceable to a document rather than estimated from memory. For compute-heavy work the largest line is often cloud or cluster time, which needs a stated unit price and a stated quantity.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by mapping each activity in the proposal to a cost category the funder recognises, then checking that category against the allowable cost rules. Direct costs are itemised and justified, indirect costs are applied at the negotiated institutional rate, and cost sharing is recorded where the call requires it. Reviewers compare the budget to the timeline and to the stated aims, so a figure that cannot be tied to a task is usually the first thing questioned.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Allowability, allocability, and reasonableness are the standard tests, and each expense must survive all three. Records such as timesheets, invoices, and subaward agreements support later audit, and unallowable items such as certain entertainment or lobbying costs are excluded by rule. Provenance matters here in the ordinary sense: the proposal should show where each number came from, and any claim about prior work should point to the original paper rather than a summary of it.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Funders are moving toward more explicit compute and data line items, and toward requiring a data management and sharing plan alongside the budget. Some calls now expect a justification for large model training runs, including energy and storage costs, and agencies increasingly ask for plain statements of what will be released and when. The direction is toward budgets that are auditable at the level of individual resources rather than broad categories.
